(1) self supervised temporal synchronization is a powerful pretext task for learning audio visual representations; (2) a curriculum learning approach with a carefully selected negative sampling scheme and the use of the InfoNCE loss are essential to obtain strong self supervised audio visual representations; and (3) the learned audio and visual features are general and effective for downstream tasks such as audio classification and action recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions: • We propose a novel curriculum learning scheme that leverages the temporal alignment between the visual and audio modalities to learn general and transferable features.

the following question: Can we learn general and effective representations for audio and video analysis by training on self supervised temporal synchronization of audio and video? We provide evidence that the answer is yes and that our approach is a promising direction for future research.
the development of effective self-supervised learning techniques for the joint learning of audio and video representations, with a particular focus on temporal synchronization.

our self-supervised pre-training scheme is a powerful tool that allows to obtain state-of-the-art results on audio and video tasks without any further fine-tuning.

we propose a new method that learns audio and video representations jointly, by training on audio video pairs that are temporally synchronized, and by leveraging a contrastive loss that is designed for this task, and that this method outperforms the state of the-art on audio and video benchmarks.
our method is able to learn general audio visual representations from self supervised temporal alignment, and that it is a very effective initialization for audio and video based tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

self supervision can provide a very effective way for training audio and visual representations from unlabeled data, and that the combination of audio and video information can provide a significant boost in performance for both tasks.

our method is a powerful tool for learning multi sensory representations from self supervision, and that it is a very effective initialization for downstream tasks in both the audio and video domains.
we propose a novel self supervised learning scheme that leverages the temporal correlation between audio and video to learn effective representations for both.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful design of the self supervised pretext task and of the training curriculum can yield effective representations for downstream tasks, even without finetuning.
self supervision can yield powerful multi sensory representations that are effective for both audio and visual analysis.
the combination of self supervised audio and video representations can be a powerful alternative to supervised learning in a number of audio and video related tasks.
